about: Lesson 7 (What does electricity cost to make?): inputs of the levelized-cost calculator and the tornado chart, and the settings of the 'when the energy arrives' step. All money is in real 2025 dollars (no inflation inside the calculation). The calculator leaves out taxes, tax credits, depreciation, interest during construction, transmission and degradation, so its results are not the agencies' own LCOE figures.

wind.label: Onshore wind farm
wind.cfNote: 33.8%: average of U.S. wind plants in 2025. Range 25-43%: the low end is illustrative; 43% is the 2023 market-average new turbine in the 2025 ATB.

solar.label: Solar farm (single-axis tracking)
solar.cfNote: 24.0%: average of U.S. solar photovoltaic plants in 2025. Range 19.4-31.5%: the weakest and best resource classes in the 2025 ATB (2023 values).

cc.label: Gas combined-cycle plant
cc.cfNote: 58.7%: average of U.S. combined-cycle plants in 2025. Range 40-80%: illustrative.

peaker.label: Gas peaker (combustion turbine)
peaker.cfNote: 13.6%: average of U.S. gas turbines in 2025 (EIA's own LCOE uses 10% for peakers). Range 5-25%: illustrative.

units.capex: $ per kW of capacity, total overnight cost (no interest during construction)
units.fom: $ per kW per year (fixed operation and maintenance)
units.heatRate: MMBtu of gas per MWh (EIA's Btu/kWh divided by 1,000)

finance.waccNote: 4% real: a round value inside the 2025 ATB's range. The ATB uses a nominal after-tax WACC of 5.6-6.5% for renewables and 6.9% for natural gas, with 2.5% inflation: about 3.0-4.3% real. Range 2-7% real: illustrative.
finance.lifeNote: 30 years: the cost recovery period in both the 2025 ATB and EIA's AEO2026 levelized costs. Range 20-40 years: illustrative.
finance.blendNote: Debt at 5% and equity at 10% (nominal) are illustrative; inflation 2.5% is the 2025 ATB's assumption.

fuel.gasNote: $3.85/MMBtu: average cost of natural gas to U.S. power plants in 2025. Range: the lowest (2020) and highest (2022) annual averages of 2015-2025, in the dollars of each year.

tornadoRanges.note: Capital cost and fixed O&M: plus or minus 25%, illustrative.

blindspot.about: Prairie Town's hottest day: the 2025 summer day with the highest hourly demand on the Southwest Power Pool grid (town_days.json, from EIA-930). Demand = shape x 450 MW (lesson 0's scale), wind = shape x 150 MW, solar = shape x farm size, each rounded to whole MW. Each hour, one more MWh saves the running cost of the most expensive plant still needed (town.json, illustrative): $0 if wind and sun are already being spilled, $40 if the combined-cycle plant is the last one running, $100 if the peaker is.
